notes: Strongest moment: turn 11, where the examiner surfaced the collision by quoting both claims verbatim side by side, traced its knock-on effect to the earlier scaling argument, and asked which one gives rather than declaring the idea wrong — the framing stayed on the claims colliding, not the person conceding. Question types were genuinely varied (clarification, assumption-probing, implications, evidence-thresholds, alternative viewpoints, and a questioning-the-question move at turn 9) and each built on the prior answer, notably the pivot from 'upset customer' detection into the password-reset/account-takeover parallel. The user held both claims to the end ('both of those are true and I don't have a clean answer'), so 'refuted' is the honest label, and the brief records the reframe they floated without resolving it. Weakest moment: the brief's frontmatter says questions_asked: 9 while the transcript shows roughly ten substantive questions after the two restatement turns — a minor bookkeeping imprecision; also the turn-2 quote is attributed to 'Turn 2' when it was said in the user's first reply, a labeling offset rather than an altered quote (the words themselves are reproduced exactly).
